questions.question_text:
A network has a maximum flow capacity of $420\text{ L/min}$.
The required peak demand is $460\text{ L/min}$.
What is the shortfall of the network?

options.why: Confused shortfall (capacity < demand) with a surplus of capacity.
Doubled the shortfall due to an arithmetic error.
Incorrectly claimed the network meets demand when $420 < 460$.

questions.question_text:
A manager wants to increase the maximum flow of a distribution network.
Which edge must be upgraded?

options.text: An edge that belongs to the minimum cut.
The edge with the smallest capacity in the entire network.
options.why: Assumed the smallest edge anywhere is automatically on the minimum cut.

options.text: The edge with the highest capacity in the entire network.
options.why: Assumed the largest edge determines overall flow increases.

options.text: Any edge directly connected to the sink vertex.
options.why: Believed only edges entering the sink can increase flow.

questions.solution_text: Only increasing the capacity of an edge on the minimum cut bottleneck can increase the overall maximum flow.

questions.question_text:
A network has minimum cut $C_1 = 50$ and second-smallest cut $C_2 = 56$.
An edge on $C_1$ is increased by $10$.
What is the new maximum flow?

options.why: Assumed the flow increases by the full $10$ without checking that $C_2$ ($56$) becomes the new bottleneck.
Assumed the flow cannot change after an upgrade.
Added $10$ to cut $C_2$ instead of upgrading cut $C_1$.

questions.solution_text: New $C_1 = 50 + 10 = 60$. Since $C_2 = 56 < 60$, $C_2$ becomes the new minimum cut. New maximum flow is $56$.

questions.question_text:
An edge with capacity $30\text{ units}$ currently carries $18\text{ units}$ of flow.
Its capacity is reduced to $22\text{ units}$.
What is the effect on the network's maximum flow?

options.text: Maximum flow is unchanged because the new capacity ($22$) still exceeds the utilised flow ($18$).

options.why: Subtracted the capacity reduction ($30 - 22 = 8$) directly from the maximum flow.
Subtracted the remaining slack ($22 - 18 = 4$) from maximum flow.
Assumed any capacity reduction halts all flow through the network.

questions.solution_text: Since the reduced capacity ($22$) is greater than the required flow ($18$), the network's maximum flow is unchanged.

questions.question_text: Why does upgrading an edge that is NOT on the minimum cut fail to increase the network's maximum flow?

options.text: The minimum cut remains the bottleneck that restricts the overall flow.
Only edges leaving the source determine the network flow.
options.why: Falsely claimed only source edges determine network throughput.

options.text: Edges not on the minimum cut already carry zero flow.
options.why: Confused lack of bottleneck constraint with zero flow.

options.text: Upgrading any single edge always reduces maximum flow.
options.why: Falsely claimed upgrades decrease capacity.

questions.solution_text: The minimum cut is the bottleneck limiting total flow. Upgrading an edge outside the minimum cut leaves the bottleneck unchanged.

questions.question_text:
A pipeline network has a maximum flow of $180\text{ kL/day}$.
Demand is projected to reach $220\text{ kL/day}$.
The minimum cut consists of pipes $A$ and $B$, and all other cuts have capacity $\ge 240\text{ kL/day}$.
By how much must the capacity of pipe $A$ or $B$ be increased to meet demand?

options.why: Halved the required capacity increase.
Computed $240 - 180 = 60$ using an unrelated cut's capacity.
Confused the required increase with the total target demand.

questions.question_text:
The minimum cut of a road network has capacity $800\text{ vehicles/hour}$ across two roads ($500$ and $300$).
If both roads are widened by $100\text{ vehicles/hour}$ each and no other cut has capacity $< 1100$, what is the new maximum flow?

options.why: Added the upgrade for only one road ($800 + 100 = 900$) instead of both roads.
Took the next cut threshold instead of calculating the upgraded min cut capacity.
Assumed widening roads on the minimum cut has no effect.

questions.question_text:
In a network with maximum flow $75$, a bottleneck edge on the unique minimum cut has its capacity reduced by $15$.
What is the new maximum flow?

options.why: Assumed reducing a bottleneck edge has no effect on maximum flow.
Added the reduction ($75 + 15 = 90$) instead of subtracting it.
Confused the remaining maximum flow with the magnitude of the reduction.

questions.question_text:
A cooling water network has maximum flow $920\text{ L/min}$.
During peak operations, the required demand is $850\text{ L/min}$.
What is the surplus capacity?

options.why: Confused a capacity surplus with a deficit.
Arithmetic error when subtracting $920 - 850$.
Assumed flow exactly equals demand without surplus.
